# A tear-out receipt reads only the origin document, so a transferred catalog record is indistinguishable from a lost one

`Serves:` #17844's AC-5 — the instrument its largest failure class needed to be dispositioned. Not a lane under an open epic; stated rather than claimed.

## The problem

`executeTearOutStep`'s receipt reports `itemKeptInCatalog` from the **origin's** `dockModel` alone:

```js
keptInCatalog = Boolean(documentAfter.items?.[itemId])   // documentAfter = the ORIGIN's
```

Catalog ownership is **per-participant** — `WorkspaceSet` derives `preserveItemIds` from the *other* participants' `items`, which only parses if an item lives in exactly one catalog. So `itemKeptInCatalog: false` has two readings with **opposite repairs**:

- the record was **lost** — a real defect in the vessel path;
- the record **moved to the vessel's participant** — correct behaviour, and the assertion is wrong.

The receipt cannot tell them apart, and neither can a reader. Six of #17844's 43 invariant failures carry exactly that signature, and the ambiguity cost a full evening of source elimination — ten writers read and cleared — before a runtime measurement settled it.

## Why it is worth an instrument rather than one investigation

The next reader of `detachItem commit did not reach committed document truth` inherits the same ambiguity. The message names a conclusion (*"did not reach"*) the code cannot support, and the receipt lacks the one field that would discriminate. Answering it once in prose leaves the next occurrence exactly as expensive.

## The fix

A spec-side helper capturing catalog keys per participant, folded into the failure message beside the receipt. Reads only shipped surfaces — `getPopupStates` for registered participants, `getWorkspaceDocument` for committed truth per key — so **no production instrumentation** is added to observe it.

## AC

- **AC-1** A helper returns catalog keys per participant id, main included, reading only existing public surfaces. No file under `src/` or `apps/` changes.
- **AC-2** `null` (unregistered participant) and `[]` (registered, empty catalog) remain distinct return values. Collapsing them hides the transfer the helper exists to detect.
- **AC-3** The snapshot travels **in the failure message** of the tear-out assertion, so a reader gets the answer without re-running the battery.
- **AC-4** It lives beside `callWorkstationGesture` in `test/playwright/e2e/utils/`, so `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` — which carries the same message on two of its own failures — uses it without a second copy.
- **AC-5** Demonstrated on the live failing scene: the snapshot names which participant holds the item.

## Out of scope

The **repair** of `waitForTearOutCommit`'s predicate. On the tear-out path it asserts the plain-detach contract (*the origin keeps the record*) against a path whose purpose is to hand that record to another participant, so it is false by design after a correct tear-out. That change lives in `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs` and belongs to @neo-gpt-emmy, who owns that surface and raised the transfer reading first.

## Revalidation trigger

If the predicate repair lands before this does, the helper still earns its place — it becomes the arm proving the fix, showing the item under the vessel key **and** a passing test. If instead a reader shows the receipt already carries participant-scoped catalog truth by a path this body missed, close as `already-resolved`.
